_comment: Ceilings for how far the C++ engine's OWN frame (FrameScene built from the scene's project document by premation-scene, D2w) may differ from the TS WebGPU frame. A LIST OF DEBTS, meant to be removed. video-decoded-frame: the FrameScene is structurally identical and the native backend draws the TS-uploaded texel bit-identically; the difference is the decode itself — E1's ffmpeg YUV->RGB conversion (chroma siting / matrix rounding) vs Chromium's WebCodecs/VideoFrame decode of the same H.264 frame. Fixing it belongs to E1's conversion parity, not the scene builder. effect-posterize: the lut:<id> strip is byte-identical to the TS upload; the difference is the path raster underneath (Chromium draws a non-baked layer on a GPU-accelerated canvas, the engine on Skia's CPU raster: ellipse edge AA, posterize amplifies it) — the same debt and the same number as native-raster-baseline.json. effect-plexus: the bake's Canvas2D program is op-for-op the TS's (canvas_effects_parity.json); Chromium blends the plexus mesh in a GPU-accelerated float16 OffscreenCanvas, the engine in a Skia CPU F16 surface — thin-line / triangle-edge AA of hundreds of faint primitives (4.4 %, was 22 % on an 8-bit canvas). Both belong to the raster backend (E3), not the scene builder. Frames not ported yet are not listed (reported as not-ported, never failed).
